title: Performance evaluation MAP & pilot timeline — hosted vs dedicated vs private
text:
Performance evaluation MAP & pilot timeline — hosted vs dedicated vs private

['From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@avasystems.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — next steps and MAP?

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo. We’re preparing an internal MAP (mutual action plan) for the pilot and procurement team asked for a concrete performance evaluation plan: latency SLOs (p50/p95), TTFT (time-to-first-token), throughput at target concurrency, and how those metrics differ between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (isolation, predictability, autoscaling behavior).

Our initial requirements:
- 500 concurrent sessions (avg 512 tokens per request)
- p95 latency < 800ms for generation on 8k context
- TTFT < 120ms for cached prefixes

Can Redwood provide a proposed MAP with test plan, expected timelines, and any input you need from us (sample prompts, dataset, network constraints)? Procurement wants to see the plan this week so they can align budget and procurement milestones.

Sara Lewis
Head of AI Engineering, Ava Systems
[sara.lewis@avasystems.com]

[Attachment: none]
', 'From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — next steps and MAP?

Sara,

Appreciate the clear ask — we can absolutely map that into a MAP and an evaluation runbook. I’ve looped in Stephanie (solutions) to own the perf plan and test harness. High level I propose:

1) Draft MAP + perf test plan delivered by Monday (includes test matrix for Hosted / Dedicated / Private, metrics we’ll capture, and required artefacts from Ava Systems).
2) Test kickoff next Wed (we’ll need sample prompts, representative request distribution, and a short list of high-priority queries for TTFT checks).
3) Two-week test window with daily short check-ins; preliminary results by day 7, final report by day 14.

I’m attaching a working draft of the MAP + perf plan (see Stephanie’s full plan to follow). If that timeline works we’ll issue a HubSpot task and a brief procurement note you can share.

Thanks — Karthik

', 'From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@avasystems.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Performance test plan (detailed) — AVA MAP v1

Hi Sara —

Attached is the performance test plan (AVA_MAP_PerfPlan_v1.pdf). Summary here:

- Objectives: verify p50/p95 token latency, TTFT on hot prefixes, sustained throughput at 250/500/750 concurrent sessions, and autoscaling/latency tails across Hosting modes.
- Workload: 3 representative buckets (short prompts 40–80 tokens, medium 200–600 tokens, long 1k–4k tokens).
- Test matrix: Hosted (shared multitenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, autoscale with burst), Private (VPC private deployment, fixed nodes + optional autoscale policy).
- Measurements: token-level latency trace, server-side queue depth, tail latency (99th), failure rate, cold-start TTFT, KV cache hit rate.
- Data collection: we’ll push results to a temporary S3 bucket and a summary CSV (we’ll share after run).

Questions for you (quick):
1) Can you provide a 1k-row prompt set and the expected request distribution (percent short/medium/long)?
2) Any network egress constraints for Private deployment (eg: firewall/NAT that could add latency)?

We’ll plan a short dry-run on Hosted first (low-cost smoke test) then run full matrix in parallel on Dedicated and Private when resources are reserved.

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: AVA_MAP_PerfPlan_v1.pdf]', 'From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@avasystems.com>

Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance test plan (detailed) — AVA MAP v1

Stephanie —

Thanks for the plan. A few clarifications from our infra/procurement:
- We’ll provide a 1k prompt set (mix attached) and the target distribution: 40% short, 45% medium, 15% long.
- Private deployment will sit behind our corporate NAT with a single egress IP — expect ~4–8ms added RTT to Redwood’s private control plane.
- Procurement wants to see an example close timeline: purchase order and committed Dedicated capacity vs Hosted pilot costs.

We’d like the Hosted dry-run as soon as possible. If results look good we plan to move to Dedicated pilot and request a procurement quote.

Evan Torres
Infrastructure Lead, Ava Systems

', 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@avasystems.com>, Evan Torres <evan.torres@avasystems.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark run results — initial summary (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Team —

We ran the scheduled test matrix (Hosted smoke run + parallel Dedicated/Private runs for 250/500 concurrency). Key highlights (short summary):

- Hosted (shared): p50 token latency = ~18ms/token, p95 = ~92ms/token for medium requests; TTFT for cached prefixes ~110ms; at 500 concurrent sessions sustained throughput dropped ~12% during burst phases and p95 tail increased by ~35% compared to Dedicated. Latency variability higher due to noisy neighbors.

- Dedicated (reserved GPUs + autoscale policy): p50 = ~16ms/token, p95 = ~68ms/token; TTFT ~95ms cached. Autoscaling triggers at sustained queue depth threshold; observed a ~20–45s scale-up time depending on model size. This gave much tighter tail latency and predictable throughput.

- Private (VPC): p50 = ~15ms/token, p95 = ~70ms/token; TTFT ~100ms cached. Isolation reduced variance but we measured an extra 4–7ms RTT consistent with your NAT note. Autoscale behavior depends on your private control plane config — with our recommended policy (reserve + reactive scale) we observed similar stability to Dedicated but requires committed nodes for burst headroom.

Attached: avasys_benchmark_results_20260411.csv with full metrics and the runbook notes. Observations + recommended next steps are in the CSV header.

Actions we suggest for your MAP:
- Shortlist target SLOs: p95 token latency <= 80ms (Dedicated target), TTFT <= 120ms.
- Pilot recommendation: start with Hosted dry-run (3 days) then Dedicated 30-day pilot with a 2-week ramp and committed burst capacity. Private is recommended for long-term if isolation/regulatory controls are required.

Happy to walk through the CSV in a quick call.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final MAP & close timeline proposal — AVA DL-7842

Sara / Evan / Procurement team —

Thanks for the prompt collaboration. Based on Rishi’s runs and your prompt set, here’s a concise MAP and proposed close timeline: 

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Week 0 (this week): Hosted dry-run (3 days) — Redwood provides test results and summary. Procurement receives Hosted pilot cost estimate and optional Dedicated quote.
- Week 1–2: Dedicated pilot kickoff (reserve capacity) — 2-week ramp, daily check-ins week 1, then thrice-weekly.
- Week 3–4: Dedicated steady-state validation and commercial terms finalization (PO due by end of Week 4)
- Week 5+: Transition to production Dedicated or Private (procurement-dependent).

Deliverables assigned:
- Redwood: MAP document, test artifacts, final benchmark CSV, procurement quote for Dedicated and Private options. (Attachment: AVA_SIGNED_MAP_20260412.pdf — draft signature for internal review)
- Ava Systems: Signed PO or procurement milestone, confirm Private egress details if pursuing Private.

Close timeline proposal: PO submission target: 2026-05-10 (we can accelerate if procurement confirms budget). Pilot start (Dedicated reserved capacity): target 2026-04-19.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you’re ok with the timeline above.
2) I’ll open a HubSpot playbook and a DocuSign for the MAP agreement. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/7842 and DocuSign preview attached.

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with Rishi and Stephanie to review the CSV and the autoscale knobs (model-specific).

Best —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
